analysis: The PR changes docs/reference/configuration.md only. The visible changes are the 'Last updated' date (line 3, 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-24) and one row at line 441, the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED row. The patch excerpt for that row is truncated, so I could not see the new wording. The base row says 0/false/no/off keep the stock kernel, packed/rows force a kernel, and anything else probes. It also says the setting is read once per process and forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The head text was not supplied, so I could not confirm exactly what changed in that row. No code, defaults, endpoints, or controls change in the supplied evidence, so the change is documentation-only. I checked the rest of the file against the threat model. The retained SSD prefix cache (T-041) is described as default-on with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the kill switch, which matches the canonical model. The App Attest worker opt-ins (lines 230-246) say they create no local trust and extend no proof lifetime. The endpoint-resumption section (lines 150-171) is consistent with TB-011 and T-053. Logout uses issuer metadata bound to the token, which matches A-008. None of these base-side statements is contradicted by anything in the diff. Remaining uncertainty: the truncated patch for line 441. A row that changes which environment variables reach the launchd job, or which kernel is forced, would only be a performance and correctness toggle with no direct security impact. No update to the threat model is evident.
